messages:
maya: Heads-up: after enabling continuous_batching_v2 in private VPC slices, small-gpu clusters (<=4GB) are showing a p99 token latency spike for short chat requests (~8-16 tokens). Observed in prod-nyc-vpc-3.

lucas: Logs or a profiler dump would help. Any kernel selector fallbacks? :eyes:

maya: Quick profiler snapshot from last 30m (cut):
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] kernel_selector: pick cu_attn_opt_v2 -> NOT_AVAILABLE
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] kernel_selector: fallback -> cu_attn_generic (latency +120ms/op)
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] kv_cache.evict_count: 520/min
[2026-03-18T14:02:32Z] batch_former: avg_batch_tokens=42, median_seq_len=10, pack_rate=0.23
```

ryan: That looks like small requests are being overpacked up to the dynamic target and we’re thrashing the KV cache, causing kernel selector to miss optimized kernels (they expect larger aligned packs).

anika: What are the token_budget targets currently? IIRC cbatch_v2 uses dynamic_target=256 on these slices which is clearly high for short-turn chats. Could try token_budget_target=64 for constrained hardware.

sophia: Also remember: private deployments had the KV prefetcher turned off for security; so cold prefill cost is higher. Prefill behavior + high packing target = simultaneous KV growth -> evictions.

lucas: Reproduced on a staging smallgpu slice (single T4, 4GB). Perf trace:
```
$ ./run_profiler --slice smallgpu-staging-1 --route chat-short
Top hitters:
  32.4% cu_gemm_mismatch_path (generic)
  18.7% memcpy_h2d
  11.2% kv_cache_serialization
  8.9% kernel_selector_overhead
```
This confirms misaligned GEMM + memcpy overhead.

maya: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- rollback continuous_batching_v2 for private slices with <=4GB memory
- add per-slice override: continuous_batching_v2.enabled=false
- set token_budget_target=64 for constrained slices
- alert rule: kernel_fallback_rate > 2% for 5m -> auto-rollback

dev-bot: deployer: rolling config update initiated to staging (cfg id: cbatch-20260318-01) :rocket:

ryan: Also suggest queue policy change: prioritize short requests with a separate queue (route-level) so packing doesn't group many short chats into one big batch that triggers KV growth. The current single queue uses median-seq heuristic which hides bimodal distributions.

anika: I'll open a PR for the config override and the token_budget_target change. Will put a note in the private ops doc for the knob: /docs/private-batching-overrides (draft).

sophia: Small addition: quantized kernels prefer aligned pack sizes. If pack_rate < 0.5 we should bias the kernel selector to keep quantized path disabled (avoids mismatch cost) or pad to aligned width.

lucas: I'll run the token_budget_target=64 test tonight and report p50/p95/p99. If numbers look good, we can canary to a single VPC region.

maya: Thanks all. Action items:
- lucas: perf test + results (tonight)
- anika: PR for knob overrides & doc
- sophia: add kernel_selector/fallback rate metric to perf dashboard (dashboard card + alert)
- ryan: prototype route-level short-request queue policy and send design note

maya: I'll monitor p99, kv evict rate, and kernel_fallback_rate during canary. Please @mention me on the PRs. :thumbsup:
